subject: MercatoX discovery — rerank eval recommendation & pilot MAP
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mercatox.com>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@mercatox.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: rerank model fit & recommended pilot (next steps)

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Call highlights (TL;DR)
- Primary goal: improve on-site search relevance for product listing and merchandising pages; target metric is conversion uplift and a 10–15% relative NDCG lift on long-tail queries.
- Constraints: 99th pct latency target <= 150ms for single-item rerank; traffic mix includes 40% query volume from mobile.
- Data availability: you can provide a 30k labeled pairwise set and click logs for the last 6 weeks.

Redwood recommended baseline for initial validation
- Candidate model (low-risk): rwd-re-rank-3b-quant (fast, quantized; expected ~8–12% NDCG improvement vs current baseline in our benchmarking).
- Candidate model (quality-first): rwd-re-rank-7b (non-quant) for a quality ceiling check — useful for headroom analysis.

Pilot playbook (what we propose)
1) Small offline validation: run NDCG/MRR on your labeled pairs + a holdout click-based simulated eval (we'll attach the eval harness).
2) Canary online A/B (2-week): 10% traffic -> rwd-re-rank-3b-quant, 10% -> rwd-re-rank-7b; measure NDCG proxy, CTR, and server-side latency.
3) Roll decision: expand to 25–50% or iterate on prompts/feature weights based on regression flags.

Artifacts we will share in the next email:
- Eval summary PDF with NDCG/MRR on your sample;
- Prompt set v3 (candidate prompts + fallback heuristics);
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) spreadsheet with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Ask from you: please confirm (a) legal/procurement contact to include on the MAP, (b) a preferred kickoff window next week, and (c) whether you can share the labeled pairwise file via the Drive link we discussed.

I attached a short matrix with acceptance criteria and proposed blockers. Happy to adjust playbook based on your procurement cadence.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: MAP_MercatoX_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mercatox.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@mercatox.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rerank model fit & recommended pilot (next steps)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying points:
1) Latency: our infra team prefers p95 <= 100ms for any production serving; the 99th <=150ms you suggested is okay for the first canary, but p95 target is something we need to hit for scale.
2) Metrics: aside from NDCG/MRR, we need to track downstream add-to-cart rate and revenue per session for the A/B.
3) Data: we can share the labeled pairs via the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow, but click logs will need a sanitized export (we'll redact PII).

Procurement/legal: looping in Alex (cc). He will propose next steps on the MAP and SOW.

Two asks: can you include an explicit regression-detection plan for quality drift (how we'll detect false positives/negative cascades during canary)? Also, please include expected token cost and an estimated GPU-hour budget for the offline runs.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah | Head of Product, Search & Discovery
MercatoX

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mercatox.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@mercatox.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rerank model fit & recommended pilot (next steps)

Priya — quick technical notes and the regression-detection checklist we promised.

Offline eval quick results (on your sample, draft)
- Baseline (current): NDCG@10 = 0.412, MRR = 0.278
- rwd-re-rank-3b-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.457 (+10.9% rel), MRR = 0.305 (+9.7% rel)
- rwd-re-rank-7b: NDCG@10 = 0.475 (+15.3% rel), MRR = 0.324 (+16.5% rel)
Note: these are offline, label-based metrics — live traffic results vary. We attached the raw CSV (ndcg_mrr_results.csv) and a one-pager (mercatox_eval_summary.pdf).

Regression detection & canary stop criteria (proposed)
- Primary guard rails (immediate stop if any triggered):
  * Statistically significant drop in CTR or add-to-cart rate (p<0.05) relative to control over 2 days;
  * Latency p95 > 120ms sustained for >30 minutes;
  * Increase in negative canned-feedback rate > 2x baseline (we'll surface via your moderation hooks).
- Secondary checks (require manual review):
  * >5 percentage point drop in revenue per session compared to control across 3 full days;
  * Spike in returned-to-search rate for top queries.

A/B split suggestion and sample size
- Traffic splits: Control 80% / rwd-re-rank-3b-quant 10% / rwd-re-rank-7b 10%
- Minimum detectable effect (MDE): with your current weekly query volume, we estimate 7–10 days to reach significance for CTR-ish signals; revenue signals may need 2–3 weeks.

Cost & infra notes
- Offline eval: ~6 GPU-hours on a V100 equivalent for the 30k labeled pairs (one-time).
- Canary serving: rwd-re-rank-3b-quant expected to be ~0.6x token-cost of 7b; we'll provide an estimated token/GPU-hour cost breakdown in the SOW.

Next artifacts we will send by EOD:
- prompt_set_v3.json (candidate prompts + fallback rules)
- ndcg_mrr_results.csv (raw numbers + stats)
- mercatox_eval_summary.pdf (one-page with visuals)

Open to tightening any of the stop criteria — calling out the p95 vs p99 conversation is helpful.

Cheers,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Alex
